questions.q: $\int_1^2 \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\left(x^2-2 x+4\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{k}+5}$, then $\mathrm{k}$ has the value
questions.solution: $\text { Let } \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I} & =\int_1^2 \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\left(x^2-2 x+4\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\ & =\int_1^2 \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\left[(x-1)^2+3\right]^{\frac{3}{2}}} \end{aligned}$ Put $x-1=\sqrt{3} \tan \theta\mathrm{d} x=\sqrt{3} \sec ^2 \theta \mathrm{d} \theta$ When $x=1, \theta=0$ When $x=2, \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{\sqrt{3} \sec ^2 \theta}{\left[3 \tan ^2 \theta+3\right]^{\frac{3}{2}}} d \theta \\ & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{\sqrt{3} \sec ^2 \theta}{\left[3\left(1+\tan ^2 \theta\right)\right]^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\ & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{\sqrt{3} \sec ^2 \theta}{3 \cdot \sqrt{3}\left(\sec ^2 \theta\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\ & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{\sec ^2 \theta}{\sec ^3 \theta} \\ & =\frac{1}{3} \int_{\infty}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos \theta \\ & =\frac{1}{3}[\sin \theta]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \\ & I=\frac{1}{3}\left[\sin \frac{\pi}{6}-\sin 0\right] \\ & I=\frac{1}{6} \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{k}{k+5}=\frac{1}{6} \\ & 6 k=k+5 \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{k}=1 \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Evaluate $\mathop{∫}_a^{b}\left|x\right|xdx, a < b$
questions.solution:
Let,& $I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}\left|x\right|xdx$

We have,~\left|x\right|x = \left\{\begin{cases}1 & x > 0 \\ - 1 & x < 0\end{cases}\right$

Case I : When 0 < a < b

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}1 . dx = {x}_a^{b} = b - a$

$= \left|b\right| - \left|a\right|$ .......(i)

Case II: When a < 0 < b

$I = \mathop{∫}_a^{0}\left|x\right|xdx + \mathop{∫}_{0}^{b}\left|x\right|xdx$
~$⇒ I = - \mathop{∫}_a^{0}1 . dx + \mathop{∫}_{0}^{b}1 . dx$

$= - \left(0 - a\right) + \left($b - 0\right)$

$= b + a$

$= \left|$b\right| - | a |$ .......(ii)

Case III : When a < b < 0

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}\left(-$1\right) . dx = - \left($b - a\right) = - b + a$

$= \left|$b\right| - \left|$a\right|$ .......(iii)

It is clear from (i), (ii) and (iii) we get

$\mathop{∫}_a^{b}\left|$x\right|xdx = \left|$b\right| - \left|$a\right|

$

questions.q: If $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( \pi + n ),$~then $mn$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{cosx}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{cosx + 1 - 1}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}sec^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = {x - tan\dfrac{x}{2}}_{0}^{\pi2}$
$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{π}{2} -1\right) - \left($0 - 0\right)$
$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{2} -1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\pi -$2\right)$.

Now using given information~$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( $\pi +$n ),$~clearly $m = \dfrac{1}{2}$and $n = - 2$.

$⇒ mn = - 1$

questions.q: If  \left.I_n=\int_{\pi / 2}^{\infty} e^{-x} \cos ^n x d x\right]$, then $\frac{I_{2018}}{I_{2016}}=$
questions.solution: We have, I_n=\int_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty} e^{-x} \cos ^n x d x Integration by parts $\begin{gathered}$I_n=\left[-$e^{-x} \cos ^n x\right]_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty} \\ -\int_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty}-e^{-x} $\cdot$n \cos ^{n-1} x(-\sin x) d x \\ =0-\int_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty} n e^{-x} \cos ^{n-1} x \sin x d x \end{gathered} By integration parts again, we get $\begin{gathered} =-$n\left[\left(-$e^{-x} \cos ^{n-1} x \sin x\right]_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty}\right. \\ \left.-\int_{\pi / 2}^{\infty}-$e^{-x}\left(\cos ^n x-(n-1) \cos ^{n-2} x \sin ^2 x\right) d x\right] \\ =-n\left[$0+\int_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty}\left($e^{-x} \cos ^n x-(n-1) e^{-x}\right.\right. \\ \left.\cos ^{n-2}$x\left($1-\cos ^2 x\right) d x\right] \\ {\left[\because \sin ^2 x=1-\cos ^2 x\right]} \end{gathered} $\begin{array}{cc} =-$n\left[\int_{\pi / 2}^{\infty}$e^{-x} \cos ^n x d x-(n-1)\right. \\ & \left.\quad \int_{\pi / 2}^{\infty}$e^{-x} \cos ^{n-2} x d x+(n-1) \int_{\pi$/ 2}^{\infty} e^{-x} \cos ^n x d x\right] \\ \text{ and } =-n\left[$I_n-(n-1) I_{n-2}+(n-1) I_n\right] \\ \Rightarrow  \text{ and }  I_n=-n\left[$n I_n-(n-1) I_{n-2}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } I_n=-n² I_n+n(n-1) I_{n-2} \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } I_n+n² I_n=n(n-1) I_{n-2} \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } I_n\left($n^2+1\right)=n(n-1) I_{n-2} \\  \text{ and }  \quad $\frac{I_n}{I_{n-2}}=\frac{n(n-1)}{n^2+1} \end{array}$Put $\quad n=2018\frac{I_{2018}}{I_{2016}}=\frac{2018(2018-1)}{(2018)^2+1}=\frac{2018 \times 2017}{(2018)^2+1}

questions.q: The value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{- 3\pi}^{3\pi}\left|\sin^{3}x\right|dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The period of the function \left|\sin^{3}x\right|$ is $\pi,$ thus $I = 6\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\sin^{3}xdx$
$⇒ I = 6\mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{3sin ⁡ x - sin ⁡ \left(3x\$right)}{4}dx\left($As \left(sin \left($3x\right) = 3sin ⁡ x - 4sin^{3}x\right)\right)$
$⇒ I = \dfrac{6}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(3sin ⁡ x - $sin\left($3x\right)\right)dx$
$⇒ I = \dfrac{3}{2} \left({- 3cos ⁡ x}_{0}^{π} + ${\dfrac{cos \left($3x\right)}{3}}_{0}^{π}\right)$
$= \dfrac{3}{2} \left($3 - \left(-$3\right) + $\$left(\dfrac{- 1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right)$
$= \dfrac{3}{2}\left(6 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{16}{3} =8$

Let, $I = \mathop{∫}_{3}^{6}\dfrac{\sqrt{{\left(36 - x^{2}\right)}^{3}}}{x^{4}}dx$
Substituting, $x = 6sin ⁡ \theta$
$dx = 6cos ⁡ \thetad\theta$
$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{\left(\sqrt{36\cos^{2}\theta}\right)}^{3}}{{6}^{4}\sin^{4}\theta}6cos ⁡ \thetad\theta$
$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\dfrac{\cos^{4}\theta}{\sin^{4}\theta}\right)d\theta$
$= {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\cot^{2}\theta\left({cosec}^{2}\theta - 1\right)d\theta$
$= {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\cot^{2}\theta{cosec}^{2}\thetad\theta - {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\cot^{2}\thetad\theta$
$= - {[ \dfrac{\cot^{3}\theta}{3} ]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} - {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}( cosec^{2}\theta - 1 ) d\theta$
$= \dfrac{- 1}{3}\left(0 - 3\sqrt{3}\right) + {cot\theta}_{\pi6}^{\pi2} + {\theta}_{\pi6}^{\pi2}$
$= \sqrt{3} + \left[0 - \sqrt{3}\right] + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.q: The value of $x > 1$ satisfying the equation $\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}tlog ⁡ tdt = \dfrac{1}{4},$ is
questions.solution:
Consider that, $I = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}tlog ⁡ tdt$

$= {\left[log ⁡ t ⋅ \dfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right]}_{1}^{x} - \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{1}{t} ⋅ \dfrac{t^{2}}{2}dt$

$= \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}log ⁡ x - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\dfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right]}_{1}^{x}$

$= \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}log ⁡ x - \dfrac{1}{2} \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right]

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}$log ⁡ x - $\dfrac{1}{4} \left($x^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}log ⁡ x - \dfrac{1}{4}x^{2} = 0$ (as $x > 1$ )

$⇒ $x^{2}\left($2log ⁡ x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2log ⁡ x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ log ⁡ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ x = e^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{e}$

questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\dfrac{dx}{( x + \alpha ) ( x + \alpha + 1 )} =\mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x + \alpha} – \dfrac{1}{x + \alpha + 1}\right)dx$
Using partial fractions
$= {ln\left|x + \alpha\right| - ln\left|x + \alpha + 1\right|}_{α}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= {ln\left|\dfrac{x + \alpha}{x + \alpha + 1}\right|}_{α}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha + 1}{2\alpha + 2}\right| - ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha}{2\alpha + 1}\right|$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)2}{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)2 - 1}\right| = ln ⁡ \dfrac{9}{8}$
$⇒ {( 2\alpha + 1 )}^{2} = 9$
$⇒ 2\alpha + 1 = \pm 3$
$⇒ \alpha = 1$ or $- 2$.

questions.q: A function $f  \left(x\right)$, continuous on the positive real axis, has the property that for all choices of $x > 0$ and $y > 0$, the integral $\mathop{∫}_x^{xy}f\left(t\right)dt$ is independent of $x$ (and therefore depends only on $y$). If $f\left(2\right) = 2,$ then $\mathop{∫}_{1}^{e}f\left(t\right)dt is equal to$
questions.solution:
As${∫}_x^{xy}f\left(t\right)dt$is independent of~$x$, so on differentiating w.r.t.~$x$,~we get

$f\left(xy\right)y - f\left(x\right) = 0$ (since $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$)

Substitute $x = 2$, $f \left(2y\right) = $\dfrac{2}{y}\left($∵ f \left(2\right) = 2\right)$

$f\left(t\right) = \dfrac{4}{t} ($Substitute $y = \dfrac{t}{2})$

$⇒ {∫}_{1}^{e}f\left(t\right)dt$

$= 4{∫}_{1}^{e}\dfrac{dt}{t}

$= 4{\log_{\mathrm{e}}t}_{1}^{e}$

$= 4$( as~$\log_{\mathrm{e}}e = 1$)

$

questions.q: Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{sinx}{x}dx$~and $J = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{cosx}{x}dx$. Then, which one of the following is true.
questions.solution:
For $x \in [ 0, 1 ]$, consider

$f ( x ) = x - sinx$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) = 1 - cosx \ge 0$

$f ( x )$~is an increasing function

$f ( x ) \ge f ( 0 )$

$⇒ f ( x ) > 0$

$⇒ x > sinx$

Now,~$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{sinx}{x}dx$

$⇒ I < {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{x}{x}dx$

$⇒ I < \dfrac{2}{3}{x\dfrac{3}{2}}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I < \dfrac{2}{3}$

Also,~$cosx \le 1$

Now,~$J = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{cosx}{x}dx$

$⇒ J < {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ J < 2{\sqrt{x}}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ J < 2$.

questions.q: For $x \in \mathbb{R}, x \ne 0,$ if $y  \left(x\right)$ is a differentiable function such that $x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y \left(t\right)dt =  \left(x + 1\right)\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt,$ then $y\left(x\right)$ equals (where $C$ is a constant)
questions.solution:
$x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y\left(t\right)dt = x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt + \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt$

Differentiate w.r.t. $x$

$\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y ( t ) dt + xy ( x ) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty ( t ) dt + x [ xy ( x ) ] + xy ( x )$

$\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y ( t ) dt = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty ( t ) dt + x^{2}y ( x )$

Differentiate again w.r.t. $x$

$y ( x ) = xy ( x ) + 2xy ( x ) + x^{2}y' ( x )$

\left(1 - 3x\right)y \left(x\right) = x^{2}y'\left(x\right)$

\dfrac{y'\left(x\right)}{y\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{1 - 3x}{x^{2}}

\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - 3x}{x^{2}}

Integrating on both sides

$⇒ logy = - $\dfrac{1}{x} -$3logx + c$

$⇒ log ( {yx}^{3} ) = - $\dfrac{1}{x} +$c$

$⇒ yx^{3} = e^{- $\dfrac{1}{x} +$c}$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{e^{- \dfrac{1}{x} + c}}{x^{3}}

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{C}{x^{3}}$e^{- $\dfrac{1}{x}}$

questions.q: lf $f\left(x\right) = \text\sin\left(\lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{2x}{π} \cot^{- 1} \dfrac{x}{t^{2}}\right),$ then ${∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(x\right)dx$ is equal to (where, $x \ne 0$)
questions.solution:
Let $y = \lim_{t \to 0} ⁡ \dfrac{2x}{\pi}\cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{x}{t^{2}}$

Case-I : when $x > 0$ then $y = \dfrac{2x}{\pi}\lim_{t \to 0} ⁡ \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{x}{t^{2}} = \dfrac{2x}{\pi} \times 0 = 0$

Case-II : when $x < 0$ then $y = \dfrac{2x}{\pi}\lim_{t \to 0} ⁡ \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{x}{t^{2}} = \dfrac{2x}{\pi} \times \pi = 2x$

$f( x ) = \left\{\begin{cases}sin0 & x > 0 \\ sin2x & x < 0\end{cases}\right$
Now, ${∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{π}{2}} f( x )dx = {∫}_{- \dfrac{π}{2}}^{0} sin2xdx + \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{π}{2}} 0 dx = - {( \dfrac{cos2x}{2} )}_{- \dfrac{π}{2}}^{0} = - \dfrac{1}{2} ( 1 - ( - 1 ) ) = - 1$
